summary: As of 2026-08-10, Claude has no native image generation on any surface — Anthropic's own vision docs FAQ states verbatim that Claude "cannot generate, produce, edit, manipulate, or create images" (EVIDENCE, fetched from platform.claude.com). All image-out paths for Claude/Claude Code are therefore wrappers around external models, in two forms: Claude Code skills that shell out to a vendor API via a script/CLI, and MCP servers exposing generate/edit tools. The dominant skill path is Google Gemini image generation ("Nano Banana"): kingbootoshi/nano-banana-2-skill (403 stars) and kkoppenhaver/cc-nano-banana (365 stars) both generate AND edit images using only a GEMINI_API_KEY; a 1,818-star companion repo (YouMind-OpenLab) is a prompt library, not a generator. The dominant MCP paths per provider: OpenAI gpt-image-1 via CLOUDWERX-DEV/gpt-image-1-mcp (create_image + create_image_edit with masks, OPENAI_API_KEY); Stability AI via tadasant/mcp-server-stability-ai (85 stars, 12 tools including outpaint/search-and-replace, 25 free credits then $0.01/credit); fal.ai via luminarylane/fal-mcp-server (52 stars, FLUX/SDXL generation plus inpainting/upscale/background removal, FAL_KEY); Black Forest Labs Flux direct via agentic-ai-forge/bfl-flux-mcp (BFL_API_KEY, Kontext editing models, but only 1 star — Flux is more commonly reached through fal or Replicate). Replicate ships an org-official MCP server (confirmed via replicate/replicate-mcp-code-mode, REPLICATE_API_TOKEN auth); its hosted endpoint mcp.replicate.com/sse appears widely in third-party configs (LEAD — replicate.com itself was egress-blocked). Every credible path requires a vendor API key with usage-based billing; multi-provider routers exist (e.g., MohamedAbdallah-14/prompt-to-asset, "zero-key first" via free-tier models). Editing/inpainting support is now table stakes: every top candidate except pure text-to-image servers supports editing existing photos. Vendor-official docs for Google/OpenAI/Replicate were unreachable through the egress proxy, so model-level capability claims rest on the fetched wrapper repos, not vendor pages.

candidates.name: kingbootoshi/nano-banana-2-skill (Gemini / Nano Banana skill)
candidates.approach: Claude Code skill + plugin wrapping a TypeScript CLI that calls Google's Gemini image models (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Preview default, Gemini 3 Pro Image optional) via a Google AI Studio API key. MIT license; cost is Google's per-image API pricing (not restated in repo). Supports reference images (-r flag) for style transfer, edit, combine; green-screen transparency.
candidates.description_quote: AI image generation CLI powered by Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Preview (default) with support for Gemini 3 Pro and any Gemini model.

candidates.name: kkoppenhaver/cc-nano-banana (Gemini / Nano Banana skill)
candidates.approach: Claude Code skill (SKILL.md fetched raw) that drives Nano Banana through the Gemini CLI; default model gemini-2.5-flash-image, optional gemini-3-pro-image-preview. Requires GEMINI_API_KEY env var; Google API usage billing. Commands include /generate, /icon, /edit, /restore — both generation and editing of existing images. License not stated in fetched SKILL.md.
candidates.description_quote: Generate and edit images using Nano Banana (Gemini CLI). Handles blog featured images, YouTube thumbnails, icons, diagrams, patterns, illustrations, photos, visual assets, graphics, artwork, pictures.

candidates.name: Replicate official MCP server (via replicate/replicate-mcp-code-mode)
candidates.approach: Org-official Replicate MCP; the fetched repo demonstrates a 'code mode' variant where the model writes sandboxed code against Replicate. Auth: 'Set your Replicate API token as an environment variable.' Hosted endpoint mcp.replicate.com/sse with OAuth appears in third-party configs (LEAD — replicate.com egress-blocked). Pay-per-run billing per model. Editing: Replicate hosts image-to-image/Kontext-class models, but editing support is model-dependent and NOT explicitly stated in the fetched README — treat edits flag as inferred. No license stated in fetched README.
candidates.description_quote: "Code Mode" makes Replicate's MCP server much faster
candidates.stars: 4 (org repo; the hosted server itself has no star count)

candidates.name: tadasant/mcp-server-stability-ai (Stability AI MCP)
candidates.approach: TypeScript MCP server calling Stability AI's REST API. 12 tools: generate-image, generate-image-sd35, remove-background, outpaint, search-and-replace, upscale-fast, upscale-creative, control-sketch, control-style, control-structure, replace-background-and-relight, search-and-recolor. Requires stability.ai API key; pricing quoted in README: '25 credits for free', '$0.01/credit, where 3 credits gets you an image generation on their Core model' (~$3 per 100 images). License badge shown but license text not confirmed in fetched README.
candidates.description_quote: MCP Server integrating MCP Clients with Stability AI's latest & greatest Stable Diffusion image manipulation functionalities
candidates.license: badge present, not confirmed in fetched README

candidates.name: luminarylane/fal-mcp-server (fal.ai MCP)
candidates.approach: Python MCP server against fal.ai's model platform: 18 tools spanning text-to-image ('Flux, SDXL, etc.'), image editing (inpainting, background removal, upscaling, resizing), plus video/music/audio (out of scope here). Requires FAL_KEY env var; fal per-inference billing with 'free tier available' and a built-in pricing tool to 'Check costs before generating content.' Server code MIT.
candidates.description_quote: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that enables Claude Desktop (and other MCP clients) to generate images, videos, music, and audio using Fal.ai models.

candidates.name: CLOUDWERX-DEV/gpt-image-1-mcp (OpenAI gpt-image-1 MCP)
candidates.approach: JavaScript MCP server calling OpenAI's gpt-image-1: create_image (text-to-image) and create_image_edit (edit existing images with text prompts and optional masks, i.e. inpainting). Requires 'OpenAI API key with access to gpt-image-1' via OPENAI_API_KEY; OpenAI per-image token billing. MIT license. Higher-starred alternative for the same model: lansespirit/image-gen-mcp (67 stars) but its description claims text-to-image only.
candidates.description_quote: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for generating and editing images using the OpenAI gpt-image-1 model.

candidates.name: agentic-ai-forge/bfl-flux-mcp (Black Forest Labs Flux direct MCP)
candidates.approach: Minimal Python MCP server against BFL's own API. Generation models: flux-pro-1.1 (default), flux-pro-1.1-ultra, flux-2-pro/flex/max, flux-pro, flux-dev; editing via edit_image tool with kontext-pro, kontext-max, fill-pro; expand-pro for outpainting. Requires BFL_API_KEY; BFL per-image billing. MIT license. Caveat: only 1 star — direct-BFL wrappers are thin on GitHub; Flux is more commonly reached via fal.ai or Replicate MCPs.
candidates.description_quote: Minimal Python MCP server for Black Forest Labs Flux image generation API.

candidates.name: lansespirit/image-gen-mcp (gpt-image-1 + Gemini Imagen multi-model MCP)
candidates.approach: Python MCP server bridging OpenAI gpt-image-1 and Google Imagen 4 for text-to-image. Per its GitHub description it is a text-to-image service (no editing claimed), so edits flag is false. Requires the respective provider API keys; usage billing per provider. License not verified (README not fetched — repo metadata only, LEAD-grade detail).
candidates.description_quote: An MCP server that integrates with gpt-image-1 & Gemini imagen4 model for text-to-image generation services

candidates.name: MohamedAbdallah-14/prompt-to-asset (multi-provider asset router, MCP + CLI)
candidates.approach: TypeScript MCP server + CLI that routes across 30+ image models (Flux, gpt-image-1, Recraft, Ideogom, Pollinations, per repo topics) for software assets (logos, icons, favicons, OG images); 'zero-key first' means it can run on free keyless models with optional API keys for premium ones. Editing support not claimed in metadata — flag false. License not verified (metadata only, LEAD-grade).
candidates.description_quote: MCP server + CLI for production-grade software assets (logos, app icons, favicons, OG, illustrations) — routes across 30+ image models, zero-key first, validates before shipping.

findings.claim: Anthropic officially states Claude has no image generation or image editing capability — Claude is vision-in only. This is an explicit doc statement, not an absence.
findings.quote: No, Claude is an image understanding model only. It can interpret and analyze images, but it cannot generate, produce, edit, manipulate, or create images.

findings.claim: The kkoppenhaver/cc-nano-banana Claude Code skill (365 stars) generates AND edits images via Gemini, requiring only GEMINI_API_KEY; default model gemini-2.5-flash-image with gemini-3-pro-image-preview option; /edit and /restore commands cover editing existing photos.
findings.quote: Generate and edit images using Nano Banana (Gemini CLI). Handles blog featured images, YouTube thumbnails, icons, diagrams, patterns, illustrations, photos, visual assets, graphics, artwork, pictures.

findings.claim: kingbootoshi/nano-banana-2-skill (403 stars, MIT, updated 2026-08-09) is the most-starred actively maintained Nano Banana generator skill; it edits/combines existing images via reference-image flags and needs a Google AI Studio GEMINI_API_KEY.
findings.quote: AI image generation CLI powered by Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Preview (default) with support for Gemini 3 Pro and any Gemini model.

findings.claim: The single most-starred 'nano banana skill' repo (1,818 stars, YouMind-OpenLab/nano-banana-pro-prompts-recommend-skill) is a prompt-recommendation library, not an image generator — star counts in this niche overweight prompt packs.
findings.quote: AI skill for OpenClaw & Claude Code — recommend from 10000+ Nano Banana Pro (Gemini) image prompts. Smart search by use case, content remix, sample images.

findings.claim: Replicate maintains an org-official MCP server authenticated by a Replicate API token; the code-mode variant executes model calls from sandboxed code.
findings.quote: Set your Replicate API token as an environment variable. You can get your API token from https://replicate.com/account/api-tokens

findings.claim: Replicate's hosted MCP endpoint is https://mcp.replicate.com/sse (also supports OAuth/DCR), per multiple independent third-party configuration files; replicate.com itself was egress-blocked so this is secondhand.
findings.quote: id: 'replicate', name: 'Replicate', description: 'Discover, compare, and run AI models on Replicate.', url: 'https://mcp.replicate.com/sse'

findings.claim: Stability AI's leading community MCP server (tadasant, 85 stars) is edit-heavy (outpaint, search-and-replace, background removal, upscale, ControlNet-style controls) and documents concrete pricing.
findings.quote: 25 credits for free ... $0.01/credit, where 3 credits gets you an image generation on their Core model

findings.claim: fal.ai is reachable from Claude via luminarylane/fal-mcp-server (FAL_KEY env var, MIT): FLUX/SDXL text-to-image plus inpainting, background removal, upscaling — and it exposes fal's whole model catalog.
findings.quote: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that enables Claude Desktop (and other MCP clients) to generate images, videos, music, and audio using Fal.ai models.

findings.claim: OpenAI gpt-image-1 supports both generation and mask-based editing when wrapped as MCP: CLOUDWERX-DEV/gpt-image-1-mcp exposes create_image and create_image_edit and requires an OpenAI API key with gpt-image-1 access.
findings.quote: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for generating and editing images using the OpenAI gpt-image-1 model.

findings.claim: Direct Black Forest Labs API integration exists but is marginal on GitHub (1 star): bfl-flux-mcp covers flux-pro/flux-2 generation plus Kontext editing (kontext-pro, kontext-max, fill-pro) and expand-pro outpainting, via BFL_API_KEY.
findings.quote: Minimal Python MCP server for Black Forest Labs Flux image generation API.

findings.claim: No official fal-ai-org GitHub MCP repo was found: a 'mcp user:fal-ai' GitHub search returned zero results on 2026-08-10, so fal integration currently rides on community servers (or fal's hosted docs, which I could not fetch).
Local diffusion (one line, per scope): no notable ComfyUI/stable-diffusion Claude skill surfaced in any of the searches run; not further investigated.

bounds: Egress proxy blocked replicate.com, ai.google.dev, and docs.anthropic.com (platform.claude.com worked and settled the Anthropic question); I did not attempt platform.openai.com, docs.bfl.ai, docs.fal.ai, or platform.stability.ai, so vendor-official model docs (gpt-image-1 editing semantics, Gemini/Nano Banana official model naming and pricing, Replicate's official MCP docs page, any first-party fal/BFL MCP) are unverified — model-capability claims rest on the fetched wrapper repos. The GitHub MCP get_file_contents tool was restricted to the session repo, so all file-level evidence came via raw.githubusercontent.com (8 successful fetches, 3 blocked, 11 total attempts — under the 12 budget). Star counts are as returned by the GitHub search API on 2026-08-10. Licenses marked 'not verified' where only repo metadata was read. I did not run or install any server/skill — no live testing of tools, auth flows, or output quality. Sampling: GitHub search only (top ~10 per query); marketplaces (Smithery, mcp.so, ClawHub) and the anthropics/skills official repo were not enumerated — anthropics/skills' canvas-design/artifact skills draw images programmatically (SVG/code), not via diffusion models, but I did not fetch it this session. Replicate edits_existing_photos=true is an inference from its model catalog, not from fetched text.
